question.worked_solution:
We have the function 

$$
y=\frac{(x+2)^{4}}{{({x}^{3}+2x-1)}^{3}}.
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides and use the quotient and power rules for logarithms:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{(x+2)^{4}}{{({x}^{3}+2x-1)}^{3}}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡((x+2)^{4})-\operatorname{ln}⁡({({x}^{3}+2x-1)}^{3}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+2)-3\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3}+2x-1)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+2))-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3}+2x-1)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =4\cdot \frac{1}{x+2}-3\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{3}+2x-1}\cdot (3{x}^{2}+2) \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =\frac{4}{x+2}-\frac{3(3{x}^{2}+2)}{{x}^{3}+2x-1} \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =\frac{4}{x+2}-\frac{9{x}^{2}+6}{{x}^{3}+2x-1}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for ${y}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y(\frac{4}{x+2}-\frac{9{x}^{2}+6}{{x}^{3}+2x-1})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=\frac{(x+2)^{4}}{{({x}^{3}+2x-1)}^{3}}:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\frac{(x+2)^{4}}{{({x}^{3}+2x-1)}^{3}}(\frac{4}{x+2}-\frac{9{x}^{2}+6}{{x}^{3}+2x-1}) \\  & =\frac{(x+2)^{4}}{{({x}^{3}+2x-1)}^{3}}(\frac{4({x}^{3}+2x-1)-(x+2)(9{x}^{2}+6)}{(x+2)({x}^{3}+2x-1)}) \\  & =\frac{(x+2)^{4}}{{({x}^{3}+2x-1)}^{3}}(\frac{-5{x}^{3}-18{x}^{2}+2x-16}{(x+2)({x}^{3}+2x-1)}) \\  & =\frac{(x+2)^{3}(-5{x}^{3}-18{x}^{2}+2x-16)}{{({x}^{3}+2x-1)}^{4}}\end{aligned}
$$
